Science at a Glance.

THE THREE LEVELS

Start at Level 1, then wonder your way up.

Every sheet wears a level pill so tonight’s pick takes one glance. The levels are a suggested order, not a rule — the question your child asked at breakfast is always the right sheet.

  1. 01

    Level 1 · Name it

    Point and name. One big picture, big friendly words, zero reading needed — the sheets a two-year-old can lead.

  2. 02

    Level 2 · Tell it

    Tell the story back. Life cycles, the water cycle, food chains: your child says what happens next, in order.

  3. 03

    Level 3 · Ask why

    Ask why together. The bigger-idea sheets — DNA, gravity, the pH scale — best with a grown-up asking the questions.

THE IDEA

Why science at a glance works.

Young children meet science the way they meet everything: one picture at a time. A volcano erupting, a caterpillar turning into a butterfly, the moon changing its shape — these printable science posters for preschool and kindergarten put one big idea on each sheet, labeled and drawn friendly, so a two-year-old can point and a five-year-old can explain.

That is also how early STEM sticks at home. Pointing builds words, words build questions, and questions build the homeschool science lesson you did not have to plan. Keep a couple of sheets on the fridge, rotate them with the seasons, and let your child catch you being curious too.

New here? This page pairs with First Glance — 58 first-word sheets in the same point-and-name style — and with the hands-on classes on the Learning Path. One sheet, one minute, one big idea: that is the whole method.

How to use the sheets.

01

Point and name

Open a sheet and name what you see, then let your child point and name it back. Echoing is learning — the volcano wants to be called by name.

02

Ask the little question

“Where is the rain going?” “Which one is Mars?” One small question turns naming into thinking, and every answer deserves a follow-up.

03

Do the tiny version

Floating soap at bath time, a magnet around the kitchen, a bean in a cup — every sheet has a two-minute experiment hiding in it.

04

Print and post

Download the full-size sheet or hit Print for a clean single-card page. The kitchen wall, the car door, the science center at co-op — science loves a good spot.
